Subject: Quantized tier pricing & demo request

Hi Karthik,

We are evaluating cost reduction options for inference across our summarization and reranking pipelines. Our infra team is particularly interested in 8-bit/4-bit quantized runtimes that keep latency within 1.5x of current p95 while reducing token costs.

Questions:
- Do you have a quantized-specific tier or SKU that ships with measurable SLOs?
- What fallback behavior do you recommend if quality regresses (auto-fallback to FP16 model? throttled routing?)
- Any standard concession/credit structure you offer for a 4–6 week PoC to validate latency/quality tradeoffs?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@medbyte.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quantized tier pricing & demo request

Hi Alicia — great to hear from you and thanks for the SOC doc. High-level options we typically propose (shortened):

1) Quantized-Light (best-effort)
   - 8-bit quantized variant on our hosted runtime
   - Target p95 latency: <= 1.4x of baseline; no hard SLA
   - Pricing: $0.0006 / token equivalent (quantized unit)
   - Fallback: soft routing to same quantized model in another region; manual rollback to FP16 promoted by ops

2) Quantized-Core (recommended for pilots)
   - 8-bit with KV-cache preservation and conservative quant kernels
   - Measured p95 SLO: <= 1.5x baseline; we can commit to SLO tracking and alerts
   - Pricing: $0.0009 / token equivalent; includes prefix caching and monitoring
   - Fallback: automated stepdown to a verified FP16 variant if KL divergence / eval set regression crosses threshold; automatic routing to dedicated pool on sustained degradation

3) Quantized-Plus (dedicated)
   - Dedicated capacity with constrained tail latency SLAs; quantization profile tuned by Redwood research
   - Pricing: custom (dependent on commit); typically ~20–30% lower unit cost at scale vs hosted Core
   - Fallback: instant failover to hot-standby FP16 nodes (SLA-backed)

PoC concessions we can offer for a 4–6 week experiment: one-time PoC credit (applied to usage) + up to 15% first-year discount if you commit to 12 months after successful pilot. Ben (cc) can confirm flex on the numbers.

I attached a short options playbook that maps tradeoffs and rollback patterns. Can you do 30 minutes on Thursday or Friday (your local time) for a quick walkthrough + show of our quantized telemetry?

Attachment: redwood_quantized_options_v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quantized tier pricing & demo request

Alicia — quick note on commercial flexibility from my side:

- For a short PoC (4–6 weeks) we can provide a $7,500 usage credit to cover engineering/eval cost.
- If MedByte signs a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot close, we can provide a 10% discount on unit pricing for Year 1 (quantized-core only).
- If you need a stricter rollback SLA (e.g., <30 minutes for automated failover), that requires a dedicated capacity add-on — we can include a trial window for that but it'll be priced separately.

Tradeoff guidance: if your priority is lowest unit cost and you're comfortable with occasional manual rollbacks, Quantized-Light is fine. If you want automated quality protection and lower operational overhead, start with Quantized-Core.

Happy to put numbers in a simple term sheet once we align on pilot scope.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Alicia / team — thanks, quick consolidation and proposed next steps:

1) Deliverables we will share before the demo (by EOD Thursday):
   - Failure-mode / rollback matrix (metrics, thresholds, automated action, expected RTO)
   - Candidate eval prompt set + scoring rubric for MedByte to run locally
   - Detailed PoC term sheet (credits, discount triggers, what credits cover)

2) PoC commercial outline (draft):
   - 6-week Quantized-Core pilot
   - $7,500 usage credit applied to any Redwood-hosted usage during pilot (does not cover 3rd-party egress/storage) — if you need coverage for that we can add a one-time infrastructure stipend (let's discuss).
   - Success criteria: maintain average QA score within 2% of baseline on your eval set and p95 latency <= 1.5x baseline for > 90% of requests during steady-state window.
   - If success: option to convert to 12-month committed Quantized-Core plan with 10% Year 1 discount.

3) Rollback / safety net approach (summary):
   - Automated regression detection (KL divergence + evaluation failure rate) -> immediate routing to hot FP16 variant for affected routes (expected RTO 5–15 minutes depending on cache warmup).
   - If degradation persists > 30 minutes -> escalate to ops + rollback to dedicated FP16 pool (RTO SLA depends on dedicated add-on).

4) Next steps:
   - Demo Friday 13:30 PT — we'll walk through telemetry and the rollback matrix.
   - We'll drop the docs and term sheet in the Drive link and HubSpot HB-45219.
